ai.description: Cantor's Kukri Snake reaches 70–90 cm. It is brownish-grey with dark, V-shaped dorsal markings and a distinct dark chevron on the nape. The belly is white with dark lateral spots.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Oligodon cyclurus* is best distinguished by the distinct, dark V-shaped or chevron-like marking on the nape of its neck, which contrasts sharply with its patterned body.
ai.habitat: Oligodon cyclurus inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests, often found in leaf litter or near streams at elevations ranging from sea level up to 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Cantor's Kukri Snake is primarily nocturnal and uses its specialized, blade-like teeth to slice into reptile eggs, allowing it to feed on the contents.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Oligodon cyclurus* is oviparous, laying clutches of 6–12 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the pre-monsoon and monsoon months, from April to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Oligodon cyclurus* is found in Northeast India, primarily across the Himalayan foothills and plains of Assam, West Bengal, and Arunachal Pradesh at low elevations.
